I farm 40 mu, that is a lot for just me and my family. My wife helps and my son helps when he can. We have wheat in winter and maize in summer, same as everyone around here in Quzhou.

Last year I did alright. My wheat gave me about 500 kg each mu, the maize maybe 550. I will do mostly the same this year. My neighbor Old Wang got better maize last year, he used that new seed from the shop in town, so I will try the same hybrid he used. For wheat I stick with the improved seed the dealer sells — everyone buys it, it grows well here.

For fertilizer, I go by bags. For wheat before planting I put down compound fertilizer, about 2 bags each mu — that is around 50 kg of the 15-15-15 compound. Then in spring when the wheat turns green I top dress with urea, about half a bag each mu, maybe 20 kg. That gives me around 22 kg of nitrogen each mu total. I would rather put a little extra than see yellow leaves — yellow leaves mean hungry wheat and empty pockets come harvest.

For maize I do the same way. One bag of compound at planting, then urea when the maize is knee-high. Around 20 kg nitrogen each mu. Maize is hungry, it grows fast in the summer heat.

Water — I have the well so I am lucky. Wheat needs water bad in winter before freeze, again when it turns green in spring, and again when the grain is filling. So 3 times for wheat, sometimes 4 if spring is dry. Maize I water 2 times usually, when I plant and once more if no rain in July.

Pesticide I spray when I see bugs or when neighbors spray. For wheat 2 times — once for aphids, once for the disease on the head. For maize 2 times also, for the borer and weeds. I do not like spraying more than needed, the chemicals cost money and burn my nose.

I use the rotary tiller, I pay the man with the machine. Plowing deep costs more and my land is not hard, rotary is enough.
